But the ONE discriminator between H1 and H3 is still UNMEASURED, and it is the same gap flagged in round 1: the ~140/min slow_queries plateau is ~46x the ~3/min implied by the logged trade scans (F28/F29), so the bulk of the counter is NOT obviously the trades query, and there is no per-application_name split of the ~190 connections / ~95% CPU / counter. Two cheap, obtainable queries could close the gap decisively: (a) finer-than-6-minute ledger-db load and any pre-08:54Z ramp (kills or supports H3's latent-saturation reading), and (b) whether the trades query's true execution rate (not the 3/min log-truncated count) is high enough to account for the counter plateau.
